values.description: Somnath, also known as Prabhas Patan, is a coastal pilgrimage destination near Veraval. Visitors come to the Somnath Jyotirlinga temple and nearby sites associated with Krishna.

records.notes: Destination metadata; no destination-wide admission fee inferred.

values.description: The Somnath temple at Prabhas Patan is a Shiva pilgrimage shrine traditionally regarded as the first of the twelve Jyotirlingas.
values.best_time_note: Trust provides wheelchairs and golf carts at the main gate and a lift inside the premises. Darshan 06:00-22:00; aarti 07:00, 12:00 and 19:00. Electronic devices must be left in lockers.

records.notes: Official trust confirms mobility facilities; this boolean covers temple visitor access, not surrounding routes or beach. Closing time corrected from 21:00. Free entrance independently confirmed.

values.description: Bhalka Tirth commemorates the traditional account of Krishna being struck by a hunter's arrow near Prabhas Patan.

records.notes: Religious tradition is attributed, not asserted as verified historical event. Accessibility still unknown.

values.description: Triveni Sangam is the pilgrimage ghat where the Hiran, Kapila and Saraswati rivers are traditionally identified as meeting the Arabian Sea.
values.best_time_note: The visitor area includes stepped ghats. Wheelchair access to the water is unverified.

records.notes: Do not import the tourism page's apparent Prayagraj Kumbh/Magh Mela copy into Somnath metadata.

values.description: Somnath Beach is the sandy shore beside the Somnath temple area on Gujarat's Arabian Sea coast.

records.notes: Mapped beach confirmed. No wheelchair suitability or swimming safety inferred.
